# Configuration reference

Raggie is configured through environment variables. The canonical list, with
safe defaults, is [`.env.example`](../.env.example); this page is generated
from it (230 variables). `make env` copies it to `.env`; `install.sh`
generates every secret for you.

> **Production:** set `RAGGIE_ENV=production` (the installer does). Outside
> development every service refuses to start with default, placeholder or
> short secrets. See [production.md](production.md).

Columns: **Default** is the value shipped in `.env.example` (*(empty)* means
unset; most services then use a built-in default described in the notes).
Variables marked *optional* are commented out in `.env.example`.

## Deployment

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RAGGIE_ENV` | `development` | development \| production. Unset or any value other than development/dev/local/ test/testing is treated as PRODUCTION: every service then refuses to boot with default, placeholder ("change-me…") or short (&lt;32 byte) secrets. install.sh sets production and generates every secret. NOTE: local, test and testing relax the secret checks exactly like development (CI and the test suites run that way). Never use any of them on a server that is reachable by anyone but you. |
| `COMPOSE_PROFILES` | `core` | core, plus optional mock \| ollama \| mcp |

## Front door (Caddy)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RAGGIE_DOMAIN` | *(empty)* | Caddy is the only service published on public interfaces: it serves the web app and the public edge paths (widget, chat stream) from ONE origin, and overwrites X-Forwarded-For with the real client IP (rate limits can't be spoofed). Empty `RAGGIE_DOMAIN` = plain HTTP on `HTTP_PORT` (local / LAN). Set it to serve https://&lt;domain&gt; with automatic Let's Encrypt (ports 80 and 443 must be reachable from the internet); then also set `ENABLE_HSTS=true.` |
| `ACME_EMAIL` | *(empty)* | optional, for Let's Encrypt expiry notices |
| `HTTP_PORT` | `80` |  |
| `HTTPS_PORT` | `443` |  |

## Web (Next.js)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WEB_PORT` | `3000` | loopback-only debug port (http://127.0.0.1:3000) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_LOCALE` | `en` | en \| tr — default UI language |
| `DEFAULT_LOCALE` | *(empty)* | Default language for newly created users, and the fallback for edge error messages and LLM prompt templates when a request carries no locale (empty = `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_LOCALE`). Answers always follow the language of the user's question. |
| `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` | `UTC` | IANA timezone for new users and scheduled tasks that don't pick one (the web pre-fills the browser's zone). Existing users/tasks keep their timezone. |
| `COOKIE_SECURE` | *(empty)* | Empty = secure automatically in production, insecure in development. Set false only for an intentional plain-HTTP deployment (no `RAGGIE_DOMAIN`, opened via a LAN IP) — otherwise production login fails because cookies require HTTPS. |
| `CONTROL_PLANE_URL` | `http://control-plane:8000` | Server-side base URL for the control-plane API (used by server actions): |
| `EDGE_URL` | `http://edge:8080` | Server-side base URL the Next.js /api/chat proxy uses to reach the Go edge: |
| `WIDGET_EMBED_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost` | Public origin where the widget loader (embed.js) is served (onboarding snippet). This is the Caddy origin: http://localhost locally, https://&lt;`RAGGIE_DOMAIN`&gt; in production. The edge port itself is not public. |
| `ENABLE_HSTS` | `false` | Send Strict-Transport-Security on page responses. Enable ONLY when the site is served over HTTPS (read at runtime, so prebuilt images honour it). |
| `PUBLIC_WEB_URL` | *(empty)* | Optional comma-separated public origins accepted by the web API CSRF origin check. Only needed when a reverse proxy rewrites Host without X-Forwarded-Host. |

## Go chat/RAG edge

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EDGE_PORT` | `8080` | edge's own listen port inside the container |
| `EDGE_HOST_PORT` | `8080` | loopback-only debug port on the host |
| `EDGE_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` |  |
| `EDGE_MAX_SSE_CONNECTIONS` | `12500` | Max concurrent chat SSE streams per edge replica. Past it a new chat gets a retryable 503 `busy` (Retry-After: 1) before any stream byte; 0 = unlimited. Metrics: raggie_edge_sse_streams / _limit / _rejected_total. |
| `EDGE_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `3` | Overall budget for dependency checks served by edge /readyz: |
| `EDGE_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` | `25` | Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM /readyz flips to 503, in-flight SSE answers may finish for this long, then remaining streams get a `reconnect` event. Keep it below the orchestrator grace period minus ~3s (k8s default grace = 30s). |
| `EDGE_SHUTDOWN_DELAY_SECONDS` | `0` | Seconds to keep serving new streams after SIGTERM while readiness already fails, so load-balancer endpoint removal propagates (preStop-sleep replacement; k8s: 5). Boot warns when delay + drain + 3s does not fit the grace period below. |
| `EDGE_TERMINATION_GRACE_SECONDS` | `30` | set to the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds |
| `METRICS_ADDR` | `127.0.0.1:9090` | Prometheus /metrics is served on a separate, internal-only listener (never on the public port). Use :9090 for in-cluster scraping; `METRICS_TOKEN` (optional) requires "Authorization: Bearer &lt;token&gt;" on /metrics. |
| `METRICS_TOKEN` | *(empty)* | also guards control-plane GET /metrics when set (&gt;=32 bytes) |
| `CHAT_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `22020096` | Max chat request body. 21 MiB fits 4 inline images of 5 MB; use 262144 if image attachments are not used. |
| `STREAM_REASONING` | `false` | Relay the model's raw chain-of-thought on the SSE `thinking` channel. Off by default: reasoning can echo retrieved content or prompt internals. |
| `HISTORY_MAX_MESSAGES` | `16` | Stored messages the edge replays as conversation history on each turn (newest first; 0 disables history). Client-sent history on a new conversation is capped the same way. Code default 16. *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | Valkey/Redis-backed sliding-window rate limits (fail-open if it is unavailable). |
| `RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_USER_PER_MINUTE` | `30` |  |
| `RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_WIDGET_SESSION_PER_MINUTE` | `10` |  |
| `RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_WIDGET_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `30` | per client IP per workspace |
| `RATE_LIMIT_WIDGET_TOKEN_PER_MINUTE` | `10` | per client IP per workspace |
| `RATE_LIMIT_WIDGET_TOKEN_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `30` | per client IP across all workspaces (workspace_id is client-chosen) |
| `HTTP_BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Seconds a client may take to send a JSON request body to the edge, in [1,600]. Covers the body read only; streaming (SSE) answers are not affected. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | *(empty)* | Comma-separated CIDRs/IPs of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted for client-IP rate limiting. Compose sets private ranges for the edge (only Caddy and in-network services can reach it); control-plane trusts loopback + private ranges by default. On Kubernetes set it to your ingress range. If a CDN/proxy sits in front of Caddy, configure `trusted_proxies` in the Caddyfile. *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `MCP_ALLOW_WRITE_TOOLS` | `false` | Expose MCP tools that are not provably read-only (readOnlyHint / read verbs). |

## Control plane (FastAPI)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTROL_PLANE_PORT` | `8000` |  |
| `CONTROL_PLANE_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` |  |
| `DIRECT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES` | `33554432` | Legacy multipart/form-data uploads are capped to keep the web/API process from buffering large files. Larger files automatically use resumable multipart. 32 MiB |

## Redis (served by Valkey)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `REDIS_HOST` | `redis` |  |
| `REDIS_PORT` | `6379` |  |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | *(empty)* | Empty = no Valkey auth (dev only; the port binds to loopback). When set, Valkey runs with --requirepass and `REDIS_URL` MUST carry the same password: `REDIS_URL=redis://:<password>@redis:6379/0` install.sh generates both. |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://redis:6379` |  |
| `REDIS_SENTINEL_ADDRS` | *(empty)* | HA (Redis/Valkey Sentinel). When BOTH are set, services connect through Sentinel failover and `REDIS_URL` is ignored; `REDIS_PASSWORD` authenticates to the data nodes, `REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD` to the sentinels. Half-configured = boot error. e.g. sentinel-0:26379,sentinel-1:26379,sentinel-2:26379 |
| `REDIS_SENTINEL_MASTER` | *(empty)* | e.g. raggie |
| `REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD` | *(empty)* |  |
| `REDIS_DB` | `0` |  |

## Web search fallback (Brave)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED` | `false` | Global kill-switch; also needs the per-workspace toggle in /admin/workspaces. |
| `WIDGET_WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED` | `false` | Let anonymous widget visitors trigger web / deep research (paid outbound Brave calls). Needs `WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED` and the workspace toggle as well; internal chats are unaffected by this switch. |
| `BRAVE_API_KEY` | *(empty)* |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_TOP_N` | `10` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_READ_ENABLED` | `true` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_READ_TOP_N` | `8` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_FETCH_CONCURRENCY` | `4` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `5` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `1500000` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_COUNTRY` | `TR` |  |
| `WEB_SEARCH_LANG` | `auto` |  |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_MAX_QUERIES` | `6` | Deep research mode (deep_search): max sub-queries a question is decomposed into (the original question always counts as one). Each covers a distinct angle (background, current state, key players, data, risks, examples). |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_TOP_N` | `10` | Per-sub-query result count for deep mode's Brave calls (vs. `WEB_SEARCH_TOP_N` for the single-web path). Higher for more breadth before deduping by URL. |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` | `50` | Cap on the deduped web results gathered across ALL deep-research sub-queries before synthesis — bounds prompt size and keeps [n] citation labels manageable. |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_PARALLELISM` | `2` | Concurrent Brave query fan-out. Results are merged round-robin by query so one angle cannot consume the whole evidence budget. Set 1 for strict rate limits. |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_READ_TOP_N` | `30` |  |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_EVIDENCE_TOP_K` | `20` |  |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `45` |  |
| `DEEP_SEARCH_FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS` | `1` |  |

## Personalization

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PERSONALIZATION_ENABLED` | `true` | Asker profile -&gt; prompt. Global kill-switch ON, but STILL gated per-workspace (workspaces.personalization_enabled, default OFF) and only for authenticated INTERNAL users. The per-workspace toggle is the privacy opt-in (data leaves to the external LLM). Set false to hard-disable everywhere. |
| `MEMORY_ENABLED` | `true` | Durable per-user memory (facts extracted across chats and sent to the LLM with later answers). Double-gated: this global kill switch AND the per-workspace "Memory" toggle, which is OFF by default. Authenticated internal chats only — never widget visitors. Users can always view and delete their stored memory. |
| `MEMORY_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | `8` | Best-effort extraction is shed when all slots are busy; it never delays chat. |
| `MEMORY_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` |  |

## MCP tool use (Jira, read-only)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MCP_ENABLED` | `false` | The chat LLM can call Jira READ tools via a self-hosted mcp-atlassian container. GLOBAL kill-switch, default OFF: when false the chat is byte-for-byte unchanged (no tools advertised, no MCP connection). Tools are also gated per-org by a CONNECTED `jira` integration (provider='jira', status='connected'). |
| `MCP_ATLASSIAN_URL` | `http://mcp-atlassian:9000/mcp` | Internal streamable-HTTP endpoint of the mcp-atlassian container (no host port): |
| `MCP_MAX_ITERATIONS` | `4` | Max agentic tool-calling iterations per chat (Stream -&gt; run tools -&gt; Stream ...). Clamped to 1..8. |
| `JIRA_URL` | *(empty)* | Jira Cloud credentials held by the mcp-atlassian container (the edge never reads them). Jira Cloud: site URL, your email, an API token from id.atlassian.com. |
| `JIRA_USERNAME` | *(empty)* |  |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN` | *(empty)* |  |

## Unified agentic turn

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_UNIFIED_LOOP` | `false` | GLOBAL kill-switch for the unified agentic loop. Default OFF: when false the chat handler keeps its legacy three-branch path (documents / web / deep + the MCP tools loop) byte-for-byte. When true, RAG documents are always-on grounding and web / deep / MCP become tools seeded from the per-turn request flags (web_search / deep_search / mcp_tools). With it on but no tool enabled on a workspace, a turn is exactly ONE Stream call — pure documents RAG, identical to today. |
| `HYBRID_CONTEXT_MODE` | `best` | Which grounding sources are placed in the prompt by default: best \| web-only \| all. "best" (default) = documents grounding only unless a tool is enabled. |
| `AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS` | `4` | Max iterations for the unified agentic loop (Stream -&gt; run tools -&gt; Stream ...). Defaults to `MCP_MAX_ITERATIONS`; clamped to 1..8. |

## Vision

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VISION_MODELS` | *(empty)* | Comma-separated chat models that accept image inputs; empty = vision off. |

## Tool-calling models

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TOOL_MODELS` | `gpt-oss-120b` | Comma-separated chat models that support OpenAI function/tool calling. The unified loop only advertises tools (MCP) to a model in this list; a model NOT listed never receives a tools/tool_choice payload (so it can't reject the request mid-stream — MCP just becomes a no-op for that turn). Default seeds the current default chat model so MCP works out of the box. |
| `REASONING_MODELS` | `gpt-oss-120b` | Comma-separated models that accept reasoning_effort in legacy single-provider mode. Explicit model profiles declare this capability per canonical model. |

## Chat LLMaaS (OpenAI-compatible /v1)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LLMAAS_BASE_URL` | `https://api.llmaas.example/v1` | The chat provider. NOTE: this provider has no embeddings endpoint — embeddings are served locally by the embeddings service below. Zero-key options: make up-demo    → deterministic mock LLM (templated answers with citations) make up-ollama  → bundled Ollama (local model below; CPU works, GPU optional via deploy/compose/docker-compose.gpu.yml) |
| `LLMAAS_API_KEY` | `change-me-llmaas-key` |  |
| `LLMAAS_CHAT_MODEL` | `gpt-oss-120b` |  |
| `MOCKLLM_MODELS` | `gpt-oss-120b,raggie-mock` | Mock LLM (`mock` profile, `make up-demo`). Compose passes only the next two settings to it; MOCKLLM_TOOL_CALLS, MOCKLLM_REASONING and MOCKLLM_API_KEY are read only when running the mockllm binary directly. Model ids the mock serves (code default: these two). *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `MOCKLLM_TOKEN_DELAY_MS` | `15` | Pause between streamed tokens; the code default is none, compose sets 15 ms. *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `LLM_MODEL_PROFILES_JSON` | *(empty)* | Optional provider-aware model registry. Empty preserves the legacy single LLMAAS_* endpoint above. When set, each canonical id is fail-closed and routes to its own OpenAI-compatible endpoint/upstream model. Secrets are referenced by env-var NAME, never embedded in this JSON. Models sharing a provider must use the same base_url, api_key_env, max_concurrency and response_header_timeout_seconds; that provider gets one isolated concurrency pool. Supported capabilities: reasoning, tools, vision.<br>Example: `LLM_MODEL_PROFILES_JSON=[{"id":"local-general","provider":"ollama","base_url":"http://ollama:11434/v1","upstream_model":"qwen3:14b","max_concurrency":2,"max_tokens":4096,"capabilities":["reasoning","tools"]},{"id":"managed-vision","provider":"managed","base_url":"https://api.llmaas.example/v1","api_key_env":"LLMAAS_API_KEY","upstream_model":"vision-model","max_concurrency":32,"max_tokens":4096,"capabilities":["vision","tools"]}]` |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL` | `qwen3:4b-instruct` | Bundled Ollama (`ollama` profile / docker-compose.ollama.yml overlay). Default: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Apache-2.0, multilingual incl. Turkish, ~2.5 GB). |
| `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` | `16384` | must fit ~12 retrieved chunks + the question |
| `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` | `24h` |  |
| `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | *(empty)* | Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint commonly accepts no key, so omit api_key_env. If a gateway requires auth, set `OLLAMA_API_KEY` and reference it; a referenced but empty secret is a boot-fatal configuration error. |
| `LLMAAS_REASONING_EFFORT` | `medium` | Default chain-of-thought depth for reasoning models (allowed: low\|medium\|high). Sent as "reasoning_effort". A valid per-request value overrides it; an invalid one falls back here. gpt-oss reasons regardless — this only tunes how deeply. The model streams its reasoning first; it is relayed to clients on the `thinking` SSE channel only when `STREAM_REASONING=true` (never persisted). |
| `LLMAAS_CHAT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | `64` | Bounded outbound concurrency from each edge replica to the shared LLM upstream (usually the real throughput ceiling, more than edge connection limits). The eval worker's judge has its own cap, `EVAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY`. |
| `LLMAAS_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` | Seconds the edge waits for an LLM endpoint's response headers (its first byte) before failing the request, in [5,900]. Applies to every edge LLM call (chat, web-research planning, model listing) — not to embeddings, reranker, Qdrant, MCP or web fetches. CPU-only local models can take minutes to process a long prompt: docker-compose.ollama.yml sets 300 (left commented here so that overlay default is not overridden). A model profile can override it per provider with "response_header_timeout_seconds" in `LLM_MODEL_PROFILES_JSON`. *Optional — commented out by default.* |

## Embeddings & reranker

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL` | `http://embeddings:8002/v1` | The embeddings service is the single internal gateway the edge and workers call. It runs either LOCAL models (default; document text never leaves the server) or proxies dense embeddings / reranking to a CLOUD provider. BM25 sparse vectors are always computed locally, so hybrid search works in both modes. `install.sh` and `make setup` ask which mode to use; see docs/embeddings.md.  Switching the dense model changes the vector space: each profile gets its own Qdrant collection (raggie_chunks_d{dim}[_{fingerprint}]) and existing documents must be re-embedded (Admin → AI → Embeddings, or `EMBEDDINGS_REEMBED_CONFIRM`). |
| `EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER` | `local` | local \| openai_compatible |
| `EMBEDDINGS_BAKE` | `dense,sparse,rerank` | image build: models to bake ("sparse" for cloud mode) |
| `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` | `intfloat/multilingual-e5-large` | Local: intfloat/multilingual-e5-large (MIT, TR+EN, 1024-d, ~2.2 GB RAM). Cloud: the provider's versioned model id, e.g. text-embedding-3-large. |
| `EMBEDDING_DIM` | `1024` | enforced by a startup probe |
| `EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX` | *(empty)* | Unset = automatic (e5 models get "query: "/"passage: " locally; cloud gets none). *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `EMBEDDINGS_PASSAGE_PREFIX` | *(empty)* | *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `EMBEDDINGS_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` | *(empty)* |  CLOUD mode only. ⚠ Document text and user questions are sent to this provider; under KVKK/GDPR you need a legal basis / DPA for that transfer. Keys belong in .env.embeddings (mode 600), which compose passes ONLY to the embeddings service — never put them in this shared file. OpenAI-compatible base; the gateway POSTs {base}/embeddings |
| `EMBEDDINGS_REQUEST_EXTRA_JSON` | *(empty)* | Provider-specific request fields as JSON objects, merged into upstream bodies: e.g. {"dimensions":1024} |
| `EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_EXTRA_JSON` | *(empty)* | e.g. {"input_type":"query"} or {"task":"retrieval.query"} |
| `EMBEDDINGS_PASSAGE_EXTRA_JSON` | *(empty)* | e.g. {"input_type":"document"} |
| `EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `3` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_RETRIES` | `1` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_PASSAGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_PASSAGE_RETRIES` | `5` | full-jitter backoff; honours Retry-After |
| `EMBEDDINGS_RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS` | `0.5` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_RETRY_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS` | `30` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_UPSTREAM_CONCURRENCY` | `8` | upstream slots per gateway replica... |
| `EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_RESERVED_SLOTS` | `2` | ...of which these serve only search queries |
| `EMBEDDINGS_UPSTREAM_BATCH_SIZE` | `64` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_UPSTREAM_BATCH_MAX_CHARS` | `200000` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_MAX_INPUT_CHARS` | `8000` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_PROBE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `30` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_CACHE_ENABLED` | `true` | Query-embedding cache in Valkey/Redis (keyed by model fingerprint), mainly to cut cloud latency and cost for repeated questions. |
| `EMBEDDINGS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` | `86400` |  |
| `EMBEDDINGS_CACHE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `0.5` | hard bound per cache call; on failure the cache is bypassed for 30 s |
| `EMBEDDINGS_CACHE_REDIS_URL` | *(empty)* | default: `REDIS_URL` *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `EMBEDDINGS_REQUIRE_AUTH` | *(empty)* | Unset = automatic: required in cloud mode, with a remote reranker (cohere/voyage/ tei) and whenever `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` is set (edge, workers and control-plane all send it as the bearer); off only for a fully local install without a secret. false opts out; with an upstream API key configured it refuses to boot outside development (anything on the network could spend that key). *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `EMBEDDINGS_FINGERPRINT_POLICY` | `block_ingest` | What control-plane does when the gateway's model fingerprint differs from the one the stored documents were embedded with: block_ingest \| refuse_boot \| auto_reindex. |
| `EMBEDDINGS_REEMBED_CONFIRM` | *(empty)* | set to the NEW fingerprint to allow auto_reindex |
| `EMBEDDINGS_INFO_TTL_SECONDS` | `60` | control-plane cache/recheck interval for the gateway profile |
| `EMBEDDINGS_ONNX_THREADS` | `4` | Ingestion concurrency. Embedding is CPU-BOUND, so total concurrent embeds should be ~= core count — over-parallelizing THRASHES (and floods the embeddings service until it drops connections), making ingestion slower AND failing docs. On an 8-core box, a proven-stable config is: 2 embeddings replicas x `EMBEDDINGS_ONNX_THREADS=4` (= 8 cores) and `INGEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` with 2 ingestion-worker replicas (= 4 docs in flight). Scale at deploy: docker compose up -d --scale embeddings=2 --scale ingestion-worker=2. ONNX intra-op threads PER embeddings replica |
| `INGEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | `2` | Max documents ONE ingestion worker embeds/upserts concurrently (bounds the load on the embeddings service). Total in-flight = ingestion-worker replicas x this. |
| `EMBED_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `180` | Worker → embeddings gateway (batched passage embedding; honours 429 Retry-After). |
| `EMBED_MAX_RETRIES` | `6` |  |
| `QDRANT_REPLICATION_FACTOR` | `1` | HA: applied only when a Qdrant collection is first created (distributed Qdrant). |
| `QDRANT_SHARD_NUMBER` | `1` |  |
| `QDRANT_WRITE_CONSISTENCY_FACTOR` | `1` |  |
| `PARSER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `120` | Each document is parsed in an isolated child process with these hard bounds; the child is killed on timeout or crash and the document ends FAILED with a reason. OOXML files are rejected before decompression if their expanded archive exceeds the limit; extracted text/cell/shape ceilings bound memory and prompt-index size. |
| `PARSER_MAX_PDF_PAGES` | `1000` | PDFs with more pages are rejected up front |
| `PARSER_OCR_MAX_PIXELS` | `25000000` | per-bitmap OCR pixel budget (render scale shrinks to fit) |
| `PARSER_MAX_ARCHIVE_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES` | `268435456` | 256 MiB expanded OOXML ceiling |
| `PARSER_MAX_EXTRACTED_CHARS` | `10000000` |  |
| `PARSER_MAX_XLSX_CELLS` | `1000000` |  |
| `PARSER_MAX_PPTX_SHAPES` | `50000` |  |
| `SPARSE_ENABLED` | `true` | Hybrid search: BM25 sparse vectors (lexical) fused with dense via Qdrant RRF. The embeddings service produces them; the workers index them; the edge queries both. Set `SPARSE_ENABLED=false` everywhere to fall back to dense-only. |
| `SPARSE_MODEL` | `Qdrant/bm25` |  |
| `RERANKER_ENABLED` | `true` | Cross-encoder reranker (gateway /v1/rerank, called by the edge after hybrid fusion). Fail-open: on error or timeout the fused order is kept. |
| `RERANKER_PROVIDER` | `local` | local \| cohere \| voyage \| tei \| none |
| `RERANKER_MODEL` | `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` | Local default: Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base (Apache-2.0, int8). Higher quality, ~2x slower on CPU: BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 (Apache-2.0). (jinaai/jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual is CC-BY-NC — non-commercial only.) |
| `RERANKER_BATCH_SIZE` | `8` | pairs per ONNX pass; bounds RAM (~1 GB) |
| `RERANKER_MAX_DOC_CHARS` | `4000` |  |
| `RERANKER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `3` | cloud rerank calls |
| `RERANKER_UPSTREAM_URL` | *(empty)* | cloud: full rerank endpoint URL (key in .env.embeddings) |

## Retrieval tuning (edge)

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RETRIEVE_CANDIDATE_K` | `80` | CANDIDATE_K chunks are pulled from Qdrant, (optionally) reranked, then trimmed to CONTEXT_K before the prompt is built. `RERANK_ENABLED` is the edge-side switch for calling /rerank; LOW_CONFIDENCE_SCORE&gt;0 hints the model when the best match is weak (it still answers). Scales differ for dense vs rerank — leave 0 to start. Quality-tuned defaults: pull a wider candidate pool (80) so the cross-encoder reranker has more to choose from, and keep a richer 12-chunk context for synthesis (chunks are ~1500 chars). LOW_CONFIDENCE_SCORE stays 0 until tuned on the eval set. |
| `RETRIEVE_CONTEXT_K` | `12` |  |
| `RETRIEVE_MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOCUMENT` | `3` | Soft diversity cap. If too few documents exist, remaining slots are backfilled with the next best chunks from the same document. |
| `RETRIEVE_LOW_CONFIDENCE_SCORE` | `0` |  |
| `RERANK_ENABLED` | `true` |  |
| `RERANK_CANDIDATE_K` | `12` | Bound CPU cross-encoder work independently from the wider RRF recall pool. Reranking 24 chunks of ~1500 chars on 4 CPU threads can exceed the edge's 5 s rerank timeout (then it fails open and is skipped). 12 is a provisional default until the published benchmark sweep (docs/benchmarks/) settles it; raise it on faster hardware or with a GPU/cloud reranker. |
| `EMBED_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `8000` | Edge → embeddings gateway timeouts. Query embedding is on the chat hot path; rerank fails open (a timeout only skips reranking and increments raggie_edge_rerank_fail_open_total on the edge metrics listener). |
| `RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS` | `5000` |  |

## Auth / security

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `JWT_SECRET` | `change-me-to-a-random-32-byte-min-secret` | install.sh generates this |
| `JWT_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS` | `28800` | 8 hours (full workday) |
| `JWT_REFRESH_TTL_SECONDS` | `2592000` | 30 days |
| `REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SECONDS` | `30` | Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a rotated-out token revokes the session (theft detection). Within this many seconds after a rotation the immediately previous token is still accepted, so concurrent refreshes from several web replicas don't log users out. 0 = strict. |
| `WIDGET_TOKEN_SECRET` | `change-me-to-a-random-32-byte-min-secret` |  |
| `WIDGET_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | `1800` | widget visitor token lifetime (30 min) |
| `INVITE_TTL_SECONDS` | `604800` | 7 days |
| `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` | *(empty)* | Server-to-server secret (&gt;=32 bytes; install.sh generates it). Used for the scheduler worker → edge /api/v1/internal/run-task call, and sent by the edge, workers and control-plane as `Authorization: Bearer` to the embeddings gateway (REQUIRED in cloud embeddings mode). Empty disables the run-task endpoint. |
| `SETUP_TOKEN` | *(empty)* | One-time token required by the first-admin (bootstrap) form. install.sh generates it and prints it. If unset outside development, control-plane generates one on first boot and prints it once in its logs. |
| `EXPOSE_API_DOCS` | `false` | Swagger/ReDoc/OpenAPI are served only in development unless this is true. |
| `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` | `20` | Login brute-force protection: per-IP sliding window, plus a per-account progressive lockout (base seconds, doubling per extra failure, capped at max). |
| `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `60` |  |
| `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD` | `5` |  |
| `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `900` |  |
| `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_BASE_SECONDS` | `30` |  |
| `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MAX_SECONDS` | `900` |  |

## Workers

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WORKER_ROLE` | `ingestion` | A worker process runs one role; compose runs one container per role. ingestion \| eval \| scheduler |
| `WORKER_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` |  |
| `WORKER_HEALTH_PORT` | `9100` | /healthz /readyz /metrics for k8s probes |
| `SCHEDULER_POLL_SECONDS` | `30` | Scheduler worker: how often (seconds) it polls scheduled_tasks for due runs. It calls the edge run-task endpoint (needs `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` above; empty → idle). |
| `SCHEDULER_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `150` | Total seconds the scheduler waits for one task run on the edge, in [10,1800]; a run that exceeds it is recorded as failed (last_status=error + a notification). Must exceed the edge's first-byte wait plus generation: docker-compose.ollama.yml sets 420. Left commented so that default applies. *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `RETRY_SWEEP_SECONDS` | `60` | Document auto-retry sweep (folded into the scheduler worker — no extra service). Every `RETRY_SWEEP_SECONDS` it re-enqueues FAILED docs whose exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, ... minutes, capped at `RETRY_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS`) has elapsed, up to the per-doc max_retries cap (default 3, stored on the documents row). Runs regardless of `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` (it only re-publishes events, never calls the edge). |
| `RETRY_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS` | `3600` | max delay between two retry attempts |
| `RETRY_SWEEP_BATCH` | `50` | max FAILED docs re-armed per sweep tick |
| `STALE_PENDING_SECONDS` | `900` | Stale-document sweep (same scheduler loop): live documents stuck in PENDING or PROCESSING for longer than this (e.g. an event lost in a Valkey failover, or a worker that crashed mid-document) are re-published. Workers heartbeat documents they are processing, so active work never looks stale. min 60; must exceed `INGEST_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` |
| `STALE_PENDING_BATCH` | `50` |  |
| `INGEST_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` | `60` |  |

## Auto-evaluator

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EVAL_FAITHFULNESS_THRESHOLD` | `0.7` |  |
| `EVAL_CITATION_VALIDITY_THRESHOLD` | `1.0` | any citation to a missing source flags the turn |
| `EVAL_CITATION_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD` | `0.6` | min substantive claims supported by valid [n] |
| `EVAL_QPS_THRESHOLD` | `20` | evaluate every turn up to this throughput |
| `EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` | `1.0` | deterministic fraction retained above threshold |
| `EVAL_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Total seconds one faithfulness-judge call may take, in [5,900]. The judge is non-streaming, so this covers prompt processing and the whole reply. A call that runs out of time leaves the answer unscored (citations are still checked); it is not retried. CPU-only local models need minutes: docker-compose.ollama.yml sets 300. Left commented so that default applies. *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `EVAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | `4` | Concurrent judge calls per eval worker. They share the LLM with chat, so a single local model wants 1 (docker-compose.ollama.yml sets 1). *Optional — commented out by default.* |
| `EVAL_MAX_DELIVERIES` | `5` | Deliveries of one answer before a failing judge (5xx, connection refused) gives up and records it without a faithfulness score; until then the event is redelivered, so a short outage still gets every answer scored. |
